title: Chronicle: PR Watchtower for Continuous Throughput & p95 Regressions
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: Implement a CI-side "Chronicle" Watchtower that automatically evaluates PRs for tokens/sec and p95 regressions against an adaptive commit-window baseline and emits human-readable verdicts in the PR. Scope: - Per-model and per-sequence-length stratified metrics (tokens/sec, p95 latency) - Baseline anchored to rolling main-branch window (configurable lookback) with decay to favour recent commits - Bayesian credible-intervals + effect-size thresholding to reduce false positives - Synthetic microburst injection for PR smoke tests to catch queueing/serialization regressions - Combined score that weights tokens/sec drop and p95 uplift to drive pass/fail decisions Acceptance criteria: 1) PR feedback comment summarizes metric deltas, confidence, and suggested mitigation (e.g., rollback to quantized variant, enable KV cache warmup) 2) System runs as a lightweight post-commit job (<= 6m avg runtime) for small workloads and scalable orchestrations for heavy smoke suites 3) False-positive rate < 3% on historical replay set (Jan 2025 - Jan 2026) 4) Configurable SLOs per repo and model family (default: 10% tokens/sec, 15% p95) 5) Integrations: GitHub check, Slack alert channel, Console dashboard panel Design notes: - We will avoid a single global baseline; instead maintain short-lived baselines per model+sequence-bucket to capture workload shifts. - Trade-offs: more granular baselines reduce masking but increase storage and compute; we'll compress historical traces via reservoir sampling and delta-encoded summaries. - For stats we use a Bayesian t-model to produce credible intervals under heavy-tailed latencies. - To reduce CI cost, only run full microburst suite when quick heuristic flags a risk (e.g., >5% variance or regression probability > 0.6). Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to staging repos, opt-in for larger repos, then default-on for repositories exceeding token-volume thresholds. Monitoring: dashboard with PR-level verdicts, weekly false-positive telemetry, and a ‚learned-cases' store for postmortems.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting — aligned on objectives. Decision: stratify by model family and 4 sequence-length buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024). Assigned owners for baseline storage work.

2026-02-26: Prototype metric collector implemented — lightweight sampler that captures tokens/sec and p95 per run. Observed that 95th percentile noise increases with sequence length; decided to apply robust M-estimator for p95 smoothing.

2026-03-02: Design review with PM (Mariana Silva) — agreed on GitHub check output format and human-readable remediation hints. PM requested explicit 'cost-impact' field in verdicts; added to checklist.
2026-03-05: Engineering review — Liam proposed Bayesian credible intervals over z-tests due to heavy tails; approved. Trade-off noted: slightly more compute but fewer FPs.
2026-03-08: Built synthetic microburst harness. Initial runs found a 12% tokens/sec regression when KV cache cold-start combined with congestion; added warmup step recommendation in PR comments.

2026-03-10: First staging rollout on repo 'redwood/runtime-serving' — ~40 PRs evaluated. Two false positives flagged; investigation revealed transient infra noise. Plan: add outlier rejection by isolating CI node-level metrics.
2026-03-12: Preparing canary rollout and documentation. Need follow-ups: (1) storage compaction for baselines (ENG-312460), (2) enable team-level SLO config UI in Console (PM-402).
2026-03-12: QA checklist created. Next: add automated replay harness to validate against historical incidents and tune thresholding.
